blocking.title: A third party's same-repo PR on the conv branch passes the ownership check, so closing it fails the card
blocking.failurePath: State: a public GitHub-form project. A build is in review, and its agent-opened PR #A (head conv-<id>, base main) is open. On a public repo anyone with read access can open a PR between two existing branches of that repo without pushing anything. A non-collaborator opens PR #B with head conv-<id> and base another existing branch (pacman repos carry many conv-* branches). The next non-review step of the build finishes, either the Verifier step enqueued at the review gate or a fix or rework step. The daemon probe then runs `gh pr list --head conv-<id> --state all` (or REST head=owner:conv-<id>). pickPr (apps/daemon/src/github-probe.ts:131-137) takes the open PR with the highest number, which is #B. finishStep sets build.prNumber = #B unconditionally (apps/server/src/services/machines.ts:1806-1808). The non-collaborator then closes #B, which a PR author can always do. reconcileOne reads pulls/#B: state closed, merged false, head.repo.id == base.repo.id (same repo) and head.ref == conversationBranch(buildId). The ownership check at ci-loop.ts:550 therefore passes. The closed path (ci-loop.ts:683-692) has no base-branch or author check. After the confirming read 50 s or more later it writes the closed row, stops the build's unclaimed verify and review steps (stopUnclaimedGateSteps), sets build.errorMessage to 'PR #B ... closed without merge, someone most likely decided against the change' and moves the todo to failed. The build's real PR #A is still open. Wrong result: a user without write access can fail any review card on a public repo and stop its gate steps. The PR body states that only the build's own PR counts, and its Risk section covers only forks, which stay in review with a hint. On main the same probe misrecording only changes the PR link; this diff adds the failed write. Possible fixes: on the closed path, require base.ref == default branch, or require that the PR is the one whose head and base match the build's delivery.
blocking.evidence: ci-loop.ts:550 `if (pull.headRepoId !== pull.baseRepoId || pull.headRef !== branch)` is the only ownership gate before the closed path. ci-loop.ts:683-692 confirm the close, then `stopUnclaimedGateSteps` and `failWithMessage(cand, todoRow.teamId, closedText)` run with no baseRef check (baseRef is checked only on the merged branch, ci-loop.ts:564+). github-probe.ts:135 `const best = pool.reduce((a, b) => (b.number > a.number ? b : a));` picks the open PR with the highest number for the head name. machines.ts:1806-1808 overwrite build.prNumber on every step done that reports a probe. runner.ts:2062 probes on every non-review step (`!isReview`). GitHub Docs (Creating a pull request): 'Anyone with read permissions to a repository can create a pull request, but you must have write permissions to create a branch.'
skeptics:
I traced the path at 9ef2a0c and the failure is real.

1. The probe finds the third party's PR. In apps/daemon/src/runner.ts (around line 2062), the probe runs after every successful step that is not a review step. That includes the verify step, because verify steps are bound to the repo; only chief and confirm-gate review steps get repo = null. In apps/daemon/src/github-probe.ts, both lookup paths match a same-repo PR from the conv branch to any base:
   - the gh path runs `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all`;
   - the REST path uses `head=owner:branch`.
   `pickPr` takes the open PR with the highest number, so a later PR #B wins over the agent's PR #A.

2. The server records it. `finishStep` in apps/server/src/services/machines.ts (lines 1806-1808) sets `build.prNumber = body.prNumber` with no condition. A verify step's completion (builds.ts:1809) only writes a verdict row and leaves the todo in review.

3. The reconcile then fails the card on #B's close. In `reconcileOne` (ci-loop.ts), the only ownership gate is `pull.headRepoId !== pull.baseRepoId || pull.headRef !== branch`. #B is same-repo with head ref conv-<id>, so it passes. `baseRef` is checked only inside the `if (pull.merged)` branch. The closed path runs only the `rowKnown` dedupe and the two-read confirm through `closedSeenAt` / `CI_CLOSED_CONFIRM_MS`. Then, with no base-branch or PR-identity check, it calls `writeSystemRow(closedText)`, `stopUnclaimedGateSteps` (stops pending or `waiting_quota` verify and review steps) and `failWithMessage` (sets `build.errorMessage`, todo moves to failed). #A is still open.

4. GitHub lets this happen. Anyone with read access to a public repo can open a PR between two existing branches. The only limits are that the head must have commits ahead of the base, which conv-<id> has against other conv-* branches, and that an open PR with the same head and base must not already exist, which only rules out base = main.

5. The PR does not cover this case. Its body says only the build's own PR counts. Its Risk section covers only fork PRs, which stay in review with a hint.

6. On main the misrecording only changed the PR link; this diff adds the review to failed write and the stopped gate steps. So a non-collaborator can fail a review card and stop its gate steps.

The code trace holds at 9ef2a0c, but the attacker it depends on cannot do the first step under GitHub's documented rules, so I could not confirm the failure as reported.

Confirmed in code:
- pickPr in apps/daemon/src/github-probe.ts:131-137 takes the open PR with the highest number. Both `gh pr list --head <branch>` and REST `head=owner:<branch>` would return a same-repo PR B.
- finishStep (machines.ts:1806-1808) overwrites build.prNumber on every non-review step done that carries a probe (runner.ts:2062 `!isReview`).
- In reconcileOne, the only ownership gate before the closed path is ci-loop.ts:550 (headRepoId === baseRepoId and headRef === conversationBranch). The closed path (about lines 683-692) has no base-ref or author check, and once the 50 s confirm passes it runs stopUnclaimedGateSteps and failWithMessage. So a same-repo PR from conv-<id> to another base, recorded on the build and then closed, would fail the card while the real PR A is still open.

Where the premise fails: the finding assumes a non-collaborator without write access can open a PR whose head is a branch of the base repo. The current GitHub docs say they cannot. The 'Creating a pull request' page includes the reusable data/reusables/pull_requests/perms-to-open-pull-request.md (fetched from github/docs main): 'To open a pull request in a public repository, you must have write access to the head or the source branch or, for organization-owned repositories, you must be a member of the organization that owns the repository to open a pull request.' The REST 'Create a pull request' docs say the same. The repository-roles table gives the read role only 'Send pull requests from forks'.

The finding quotes an older line ('Anyone with read permissions ... can create a pull request'). Today that line sits alongside the note above and covers PRs from forks. Fork PRs are exactly what the head.repo.id === base.repo.id check rejects, with a hint only.

Who can still open such a PR:
- Collaborators with write access. They can already close PR A directly, which fails the card by design, so this path adds nothing for them.
- Members of the organization that owns an org repo. They are inside that org's trust boundary, which is not the 'any user on a public repo' attacker the finding describes.

Limits of this check: I could not test GitHub's enforcement myself. API access is limited to xiechimon/pacman, and GitHub is read-only for this task. So the premise stays unconfirmed and is contradicted by GitHub's own documentation.

A benign edge case remains: a collaborator who opens a second PR from the conv branch to another base (for example a backport) and later closes it could fail the card. That is a narrower correctness issue, not the third-party safety failure reported.

suggestions.title: Containment check picks the checkpoint by step creation time, not push order, so a verify step created in an earlier round that pushes after a later build step is missed
suggestions.failurePath: Round 1: build step B1 finishes with checkpoint C1 and the card reaches review. maybeEnqueueVerifyStep queues verify step V (createdAt T2), which stays pending or waiting_quota: the Verifier machine is offline (#1257 keeps pending steps) or V is held by quota. Nothing stops V on review -> planning. Round 2: a person requests changes, then plan step P and build step B2 (createdAt T4 > T2) run on the build agent's machine. B2 pushes C2, the grind moves the card to review, and maybeEnqueueVerifyStep skips because V's row exists. The PR is merged on GitHub at head C2. V is then claimed; claim order is createdAt plus eligibility (machines.ts claimCandidates), and while V runs the reconcile skips. V commits evidence on top of C2 and pushes C3; the daemon commits and pushes for every non-review step. The next sweep runs the checkpoint query at ci-loop.ts:583-596 (`ne(kind,'review'), status done, orderBy(desc(step.createdAt))`). It returns B2's C2, because B2 was created after V. C2 equals pull.headSha, so the compare is skipped, the merged row is written and finishTodoDone moves the card to done. C3 is not in the merge and no hint is written. Round 16 set out to catch exactly this ("a Verifier commit pushed after a GitHub merge leaves the card in review with a hint"). Test ㉔ is titled "the last one to finish decides", but it seeds createdAt in finish order, so it cannot tell the two orderings apart. The window is narrow: it needs a verify step that outlives a round and then pushes a commit. Possible fixes: order by claimedAt (or lastHeartbeatAt) instead of createdAt, or check containment for every distinct done checkpoint of the round.
suggestions.evidence: ci-loop.ts:583-596 selects `step.checkpointCommit` with `.orderBy(desc(step.createdAt)).get()`. step has no completion-time column (schema.ts:180-219, only claimedAt/lastHeartbeatAt). builds.ts maybeEnqueueVerifyStep skips any build that already has a verify row (stated in the PR Risk section), and sweepAbandonedBuildSteps leaves pending steps alone (builds.ts:1506). pr-reconcile.test.ts:1008-1023 (㉔) seeds checkpoints with increasing createdAt only.

suggestions.title: Semantic conflict with open PR #1468: the #1466 githubRepo guard must go into the new githubTarget, which also feeds the reconcile's pulls and compare reads
suggestions.evidence: #1468 (base main, head 0a4b003) edits ci-loop.ts pollOne. It replaces the inline `projRow.githubRepo.indexOf('/')` split with `githubRepoOfProject(projRow)`, which refuses `.` and `..` segments (#1466), and it does the same in builds.ts probePullState and completeStep. #1414 deletes that same inline split from pollOne and moves it into a new `githubTarget` (ci-loop.ts:437-450). That function only checks `slash < 1 || slash === length-1`, and both pollOne and the new reconcileOne use it. repoPath (github.ts:450) uses encodeURIComponent, which leaves `.` unencoded.
suggestions.failurePath: Merge order matters. Suppose #1468 lands first and #1414 is rebased. The conflict hunk is in pollOne, while githubTarget is a new function with no conflict marker. If the resolver keeps #1414's side of the hunk (`githubTarget(todoRow.projectId)`), the grind silently loses the #1466 guard. The reconcile's new outbound reads never get it either. A project whose stored githubRepo is `owner/..` then sends `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/../pulls/{n}` and `.../compare/...`, the path rewrite #1466 closes. Whichever PR merges second should call githubRepoOfProject inside githubTarget. Mention it in the Risk section (docs/pr-review.md, semantic conflicts).

The PR body's Risk section admits the gap: 'Round 10 added tests after the rules they cover had shipped (CLAUDE.md asks for tests first); its red leg is the mutation run', and 'Some round 14 and 15 tests pin rules that were already in place'. suggestions.title: ⑨ (two builds on one PR, #1217) moves the PR's head ref to the newer build's branch, so the realistic shape of this failure mode is never tested
suggestions.failurePath: The test calls makeWorld({ newerBuildPr: 201 }). Lines 334-337 first map PR 201 to the older build's branch with headRefs.set(201, conversationBranch(buildId)), then overwrite it with headRefs.set(201, conversationBranch(`build-new-…`)). The mock therefore answers head.ref = the newer, current build's branch, and the test asserts done with the rows written on the current build. In production a second build records an existing PR through the daemon probe: --head on the conversation branch, plus the #1195 drift and artifact branches (apps/daemon/src/runner.ts:2066-2072). That PR's head is the branch it was opened from, normally the older build's. With head.ref = the older build's branch, the ownership check at apps/server/src/services/ci-loop.ts:550 marks the PR foreign. I ran a variant of ⑨ at the head to confirm: phase stays review, reviewForeign 1, merged 0, and the card gets the 'may be a fork PR' hint. It never reaches done. This is the safe direction, and Risk says a PR opened from another branch is handled this way. Still, the test name ('written on the current build') claims more coverage of the ticket's #1217 failure mode than it has. Adding a case where the head is the older build's branch would pin the real outcome.
suggestions.evidence: pr-reconcile.test.ts:334-337: headRefs.set(prNumber, conversationBranch(buildId)); if (typeof opts.newerBuildPr === 'number') headRefs.set(opts.newerBuildPr, conversationBranch(`build-new-${rnd}`)); variant run at head: expected { phase: 'review', foreign: 1, merged: 0 }

suggestions.title: githubText strips control characters but not format characters (bidi overrides, zero-width)
suggestions.failurePath: A base branch or default branch name containing U+202E or zero-width characters, which git refnames allow, passes `replace(/\p{Cc}/gu, '')` unchanged. It then lands in the 'merged into branch X, not default branch Y' hint, which the web timeline renders and agents read through the conversation tool. Only repository writers can create those branches, so the impact is limited to misleading display text. Stripping \p{Cf} as well would close it.
suggestions.evidence: ci-loop.ts:136-141 `const chars = Array.from(text.replace(/\p{Cc}/gu, ''));`. It is used for baseRef and defaultBranch in the hint at ci-loop.ts:572-576 (the merged, non-default-branch case).

suggestions.title: No runtime evidence that the reconcile moves a real card; acceptance rests on stubbed-fetch vitest plus response-shape captures
suggestions.failurePath: The claim in Verified and Acceptance is that a PR merged on GitHub moves the card to done and a closed PR moves it to failed. Every archived proof runs githubPull and githubCompareStatus against a stubbed fetch inside vitest. The live captures were read through the agent proxy, which attached its own credentials (X-Ratelimit-Limit 15000, lines 5-7). They show response shape only, not a server sweep acting on a card. CLAUDE.md's mechanism rule asks for a runtime artifact, and ticket #1403 lists a host test. No verify-pacman live-stack run or log of a real ci-loop sweep writing the merged row is archived. A wiring gap outside the tested functions (scheduler registration of the sweep, the token lookup on the real DB) would pass every archived file. The body defers this to the host / segment 3, and pr-gate run 8 raised the same point.
